patch.value: GH-1754: cursor-named fields inside items block string compaction, so a budgeted list omits its rows (regression since 2026.11.11)

Reported in GH-1754 against 2026.11.18. The protection that keeps emitted continuation tokens replayable also exempts item fields that merely share a continuation key name (next_cursor, output_cursor) from string compaction. At a 2,000-token budget, a list whose one item carries a 30,000-character next_cursor or output_cursor field exits 2 with read_output.result_omitted true and strings_compacted false. The same request on 2026.11.11 returned one compacted row and exited 0. An ordinary_text control still compacts to a 255-character value. Only the envelope's continuation tokens should be exempt; the cursor-clipping fix is related.

A budgeted list whose item carries an oversized next_cursor or output_cursor field returns its compacted row and exits 0; An envelope next_cursor or output_cursor is still delivered intact and replays; Tests cover both the replayable envelope cursor and compaction of cursor-named item metadata

Producer and output continuation tokens in the response envelope stay replayable, while oversized strings under items, including fields named like a continuation key, are still compacted so the budgeted list returns its rows.

An item field named next_cursor or output_cursor is exempt from compaction, so at a 2,000-token budget the list is omitted (result_omitted true, strings_compacted false, exit 2) instead of returning a compacted row as 2026.11.11 did.
